content:
You can align table captions to the left in LaTeX without the `caption` package using several methods:

## Method 1: Using `\raggedright`

```latex
\begin{table}[h]
\centering
\caption{\raggedright Your left-aligned caption text goes here}
\begin{tabular}{|c|c|c|}
\hline
Column 1 & Column 2 & Column 3 \\
\hline
Data 1 & Data 2 & Data 3 \\
\hline
\end{tabular}
\end{table}
```

## Method 2: Redefining caption formatting globally

Add this to your preamble to make all table captions left-aligned:

```latex
\makeatletter
\long\def\@makecaption#1#2{%
  \vskip\abovecaptionskip
  \sbox\@tempboxa{#1: #2}%
  \ifdim \wd\@tempboxa >\hsize
    \raggedright #1: #2\par
  \else
    \raggedright #1: #2\par
  \fi
  \vskip\belowcaptionskip}
\makeatother
```

## Method 3: Using a custom command

Define a custom left-aligned caption command:

```latex
\newcommand{\leftcaption}[1]{%
  \begingroup
  \raggedright
  \caption{#1}%
  \endgroup
}
```

Then use it like:
```latex
\begin{table}[h]
\centering
\leftcaption{Your left-aligned caption text}
\begin{tabular}{|c|c|c|}
% table content
\end{tabular}
\end{table}
```

## Method 4: Manual formatting with `\parbox`

```latex
\begin{table}[h]
\centering
\parbox{\textwidth}{\raggedright\textbf{Table 1:} Your caption text here}
\vspace{0.5em}
\begin{tabular}{|c|c|c|}
% table content
\end{tabular}
\end{table}
```

The first method is usually the simplest for individual tables, while the second method is best if you want all your table captions to be left-aligned throughout the document.
